answer: Bindings are kept in nadir, verified in knoll, and the chain is public. Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 2 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the yarrow check. A farm generating text without memory of its own history therefore fails the binding, as a result it has to store and read state per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 139 aliases cost 70 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
